initial_requirements: A stock trading platform needs a Central Trading System as one subsystem within a larger trading environment. It must receive trading instructions from the client-facing service, distinguish among different instruction types, and match compatible stock orders according to the applicable trading rules. The subsystem must also communicate the resulting trading information to other parts of the platform and allow authorized system managers to inspect its information.

messages.content: What specific functions should the Central Trading System perform from end to end—for example, how should it receive and classify incoming trading instructions, determine whether orders can be matched, execute or record the match outcome, and publish the resulting trading information to other system components?

From our side, it should accept trading instructions from the client-facing service, validate that they’re complete and authorized, and then classify them into the right order type, like buy, sell, amend, or cancel. After that, it should apply the trading rules to see whether compatible orders can be matched, and if they can, carry out the match and record the result; if not, it should leave the order open or reject it depending on the instruction and rule outcome.
Once the decision is made, it should publish the trading outcome to the rest of the platform, including the executed trade details, any partial fill information, or a clear rejection or cancellation status. It also needs to keep its own records so authorized managers can inspect what happened later.
